technical_and_design_decisions: Implement U1 using the Spring Boot security starter available to the target Spring Boot 1.1.x branch rather than introducing a custom authentication filter.
Use the existing Spring Boot property server.basic.enabled, with false as the application.yml default; enabling it activates HTTP Basic authentication.
Represent single-user credentials in servers.yml and bind or translate them into the Spring Boot security configuration using the repository's existing configuration conventions.
Extend the XD Shell admin config command with --username and --password options and pass these credentials through the existing HTTP client configuration.
Treat the Spring Boot snapshot and release dependency updates as separate build-validation activities, while keeping the selected versions compatible with the legacy XD codebase.

Implement the sandbox and production Docker images with Dockerfiles and repeatable build/run documentation; the sandbox image includes Redis and RabbitMQ, while the production image includes only the XD runtime and Java.
Deliver U6 as a discovery and planning spike only; no REST archive-upload implementation is included in this increment.
Add automated tests where practical and perform focused integration and regression testing across security, shell connectivity, dependency updates, and Docker startup.
assumptions: The target codebase is the historical spring-xd-dirt/XD branch compatible with Spring Boot 1.1.x and Java 7, despite the general description mentioning newer Spring Framework Java requirements.
Existing build, configuration, shell command, HTTP client, and test infrastructure can be extended without a major architectural redesign.
The servers.yml schema and server connection model are available in the repository; only the security credential fields and related wiring need to be added.
Basic authentication is intended for a single configured user and password, with credentials stored in the existing configuration mechanism rather than an external identity provider.

Passwords supplied through the shell are handled using the existing command-line parsing and connection configuration facilities; secure secret storage beyond process/configuration handling is out of scope.

The requested 'latest' Spring Boot snapshot and release mean the latest versions compatible with this legacy branch at implementation time, not current Spring Boot versions requiring a modern Java baseline.
Ubuntu-based Docker images may use an available Java 7 distribution and existing XD build artifacts; licensing, image publication, orchestration, and production operations are out of scope.
Redis and RabbitMQ are installed or made available in the sandbox image using straightforward image provisioning, with default local-development configuration.
The REST archive spike requires documentation, options analysis, feedback collection, phase definition, and creation of follow-up stories, but not production code.
Effort estimates represent one developer's hands-on work in workdays and include normal local verification, but exclude waiting time for external approvals or unavailable infrastructure.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing XD modules, build files, application configuration, servers.yml handling, shell admin command, HTTP client, test conventions, and Docker support; finalize the implementation approach and acceptance checklist.

Add the Spring Boot security starter, set server.basic.enabled to false in application.yml, wire the property-controlled security behavior, and add focused tests verifying enabled and disabled authentication behavior.

Extend servers.yml parsing and server configuration to accept a username and password, connect those values to the Spring Boot security setup, validate configuration behavior, and add configuration and authentication tests.

Add --username and --password to the admin config command, propagate the values into the admin server connection settings, handle command validation and help text, and test authenticated shell interaction with a secured admin server.
Update repository or build configuration to resolve the selected compatible Spring Boot snapshot, resolve transitive dependency issues, build the affected modules, and run focused tests.
Update the dependency to the selected compatible Spring Boot release, reconcile any API or dependency differences from the snapshot baseline, build the project, and run focused regression tests.

Assess the customer need, investigate REST archive-upload and custom module/configuration options, document alternatives and trade-offs, socialize findings with the team, identify implementation phases, and create follow-up stories.
Create an Ubuntu-based Docker image containing the full XD jar, Java 7, Redis, and RabbitMQ; add startup/configuration scripts, verify container startup and basic XD connectivity, and document usage.

Create an Ubuntu-based leaner image containing the full XD jar and Java 7, define runtime configuration and startup behavior, verify image startup and XD execution, and document baseline deployment usage.

activities.activity_name: End-to-end regression, packaging, and delivery documentation
activities.activity_description: Run the combined build and regression suite, verify secured and unsecured server scenarios and shell authentication, validate both Docker images, update user and developer documentation, and prepare the final change set.
